profile.name: Ahsen Malik
profile.bio: Ahsen Malik is an independent candidate for Virginia's 10th Congressional District. His name appears on the ballot as Ahsen Mujeeb Malik.
profile.notes: Local coverage reports no visible campaign presence, and no website, social accounts or policy statements were found.

profile.name: Dianne Blais
profile.bio: Dianne Blais is a longtime Northern Virginia community volunteer who has been active in the League of Women Voters and served as co-president of Virginia AAUW from 2008 to 2010. She was the Green Party nominee for Virginia's 10th District in 2014, an independent candidate for the House of Delegates in 2011, and a previous candidate in the 11th District.
profile.notes: No 2026 campaign website or issue statements were found; earlier Green Party material describes her as anti-war and pro-environment, but the source page could not be loaded to confirm specifics.

profile.name: Joan Andrews Bell
profile.bio: Joan Andrews Bell is an independent candidate for Virginia's 4th District and a longtime anti-abortion activist who has been arrested many times at clinic protests. She was convicted under the federal FACE Act in 2023 and pardoned by President Trump in January 2025. Her candidacy is part of the Defending the Unborn slate of independent congressional candidates.

platform.point: Campaigns against later-term abortion in Virginia.
Urges voters to reject Virginia's Amendment 1 abortion-rights ballot measure.
Uses her candidacy to air television ads showing images she says depict abortion's victims.

liberty.evidence: Campaigns against abortion and Virginia's Amendment 1; no stated positions on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

profile.notes: Listed on the ballot as Joan E. "Andrews" Bell; the liberty score rests on abortion alone. One VPM article listed different VA-4 independents, but the state and Henrico candidate lists include her.
